findings.title: The C1 FakeRunner unification shipped consume-on-match semantics that no single consumer set can satisfy — 4 of the 8 pytest failures, and 5 red mutation control-arms, come from it
findings.location: Task 1 / scripts/brain/tests/helpers_client_state.py (`del self.responses[i]` in FakeRunner.run) vs Tasks 8, 15, 19 and Task 2
findings.evidence: C1 says 'first matching prefix wins, in insertion order'; the implementation DELETES the matched entry, so one record() serves exactly one call. Real failures: Task 8 test_backfill_query_composes_exclusion_and_day_sweep (1 +triage response recorded, sweep issues 1+days queries -> GmailSourceError rc=127 'FakeRunner: no response'); Task 15 test_two_known_contacts_same_page_one_history_two_crm_rows (1 add-interaction.py response, 2 contacts -> WriterError -> exit_code 3); Task 19 test_gmail_section_renders_each_change_line_type (1 list-tasks response, list_open_tasks enumerates human AND build -> TaskEnumerationError). Deleting the `del` line flips the suite to '3 failed, 642 passed' and breaks the OTHER side: Task 2 test_acquire_retries_once_on_stale_cleared_stderr_and_wins (the C11/G0A-20 fix) REQUIRES consumption so the retry gets the second response. Both directions run and recorded. Consequently mutation-check.sh records control_green:false for G-QUERY-1, G-CRM-2, G-HIST-2, G-MERGE-1 and G-SUPER-1 — five guards whose control arm never went green.
findings.fix: Pick ONE semantics in C1 and make every consumer match it. Cleanest: make matching NON-consuming by default (so a prefix stands for 'every call shaped like this') and add an explicit `record_once(prefix, ...)` / FIFO queue for the single genuine sequence case (Task 2's stale-cleared -> win). Then re-derive Tasks 8, 15 and 19's Step-4 counts from a real run.

findings.title: A --dry-run writes ledger rows with outcome 'filed' and writes=[], so `is_terminal` makes the subsequent LIVE run a no-op — the dry-run silently cancels the release
findings.location: Task 15 / scripts/brain/client_state_gmail.py `_file_message` (`resolution.outcome = "filed"` on the dry-run path, then `ledger.append(row)` at :303) vs observation_ledger.Ledger.is_terminal
findings.evidence: Ran the orchestrator twice against one --state-dir with the same message: DRY-RUN -> exit 0, filed 1, ledger row resolutions [{'outcome':'filed'}] with writes=[]; LIVE-RUN -> exit 0, filed 0, skipped_terminal 1, ZERO add-interaction.py calls, and the vault page still contains no 'gmail:m1' marker. is_terminal is 'latest row, same digest, all outcomes == filed', which the dry-run row satisfies. The same mechanism silences FR-003: the dry-run row makes ledger.escalated_for(ref, digest) true, so the live run never sends the Telegram. This is a direct consequence of the G0A-3/G0B-1/C7 fix (persist in dry-run) not being paired with a persisted-outcome distinction. The goal's rollout runs dry-runs before live, and G4 items 3/5/6 are produced from dry-runs.
findings.fix: Persist the dry-run row WITHOUT terminal semantics: either stamp the row `dry_run: true` and have is_terminal/escalated_for ignore such rows, or keep the resolution outcome 'pending' in dry-run and only set 'filed' on the live write path. Add a test that does dry-run then live against the same --state-dir and asserts the live run still writes CRM + page + task.

findings.title: Four registered guards are not actually pinned — their named test stays GREEN with the guard mutated away, so mutation-check.sh exits 1 and G4 item 7 cannot pass
findings.location: Task 23 / scripts/brain/tests/test_client_state_guards.py GUARD_REGISTRY rows G-RES-1, G-INV-1, G-DIG-1, G-IDEMP-2 (+ their sites in resolve_email.py, client_state_digest.py, client_state_gmail.py)
findings.evidence: Each mutation was re-applied by hand with __pycache__ cleared and the registered node run alone: G-RES-1 `domain_to_slug.get(dom)` -> `.get(dom.split('.')[0])` / test_full_domain_never_bare_label_collision -> 1 passed; G-INV-1 `domain_pages.setdefault(dom, [])` -> `.setdefault(dom.split('.')[0], [])` / test_compute_invariants_does_not_confuse_different_tlds -> 1 passed; G-DIG-1 collapse condition -> `if True:` / test_gmail_section_collapses_to_one_line_when_nothing_happened -> 1 passed; G-IDEMP-2 signature check -> `if False:` / test_second_identical_dry_run_zero_new_claude_calls -> 1 passed. G-RES-1 and G-INV-1 are the FR-004 'full domain, never the bare label' invariant on both sides of the system; G-IDEMP-2 is FR-001's no-duplicate-append rule. mutation-check.sh over 50 rows exits 1 with 11 rows not fully green (these 4 + G-EXT-2's false negative + G-LEDGER-4's stale node + the 5 control-red rows from G0A2-1).
findings.fix: For each of the four, either strengthen the named test until the mutation makes it fail (e.g. G-RES-1 needs a fixture where two pages differ only past the first label, like example.com vs example.org, and G-IDEMP-2 needs an assertion on the ledger row COUNT after the second run), or repoint the registry row at a test that does bite. A guard whose mutation does not bite is worse than no guard.

findings.title: mutation-check.sh reports false 'mutated_red: false' for byte-length-preserving mutations because it never clears __pycache__ between the control and mutated arms
findings.evidence: G-EXT-2's sed is `/CLAUDE_ARGV: list[str] = [/,+12 s/"1",/"2",/` — same byte length. The harness recorded control_green:true, mutation_applied:true, mutated_red:FALSE. Re-running the identical sed and the identical node by hand after `find scripts/brain -name __pycache__ -exec rm -rf {} +` gives '1 failed' — the guard DOES bite. CPython validates a .pyc against (source mtime in SECONDS, source size); the control run, the cp, the sed and the mutated run all complete inside one wall-clock second (the node takes 0.02s), so the stale bytecode is reused and the mutation is invisible. The failure direction is fail-closed (a real guard reported unproven), but it blocks G4 item 7 and it would equally hide a genuinely unproven guard behind noise.
findings.fix: Export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 for the whole script, or `find "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" -name __pycache__ -type d -exec rm -rf {} +` immediately after each sed and each restore.

findings.title: The PATH-trap shim traps `bus list-tasks`, which the amended goal now requires it to pass through — every live dry-run in the G4 protocol would die with TaskEnumerationError
findings.location: Task 21 / docs/pipeline/run-artifacts/client-state-gmail-v1/shims/cortextos (plan line 10858) vs goal (248d61de) STANDING RULES, amended 2026-09-14 after G0 round-2 finding G0B2-6

findings.title: A lock-held refusal writes error/failed_at INTO run-receipt.json, but the amended G4 item 5 requires the receipt byte-identical and the cause in a separate last-lock-refusal.json
findings.location: Task 3 / scripts/brain/observation_ledger.py record_failure + Task 15 / client_state_gmail.py:319 `record_failure(cfg.state_dir, "lock-held")`, and Task 21 / g4-check.sh check_5, vs goal (248d61de) G4 item 5, amended 2026-09-14 after G0 round-2 finding G0B2-7
findings.evidence: record_failure does `prev = read_receipt(state_dir) or {}; out = dict(prev); out.update(partial); out['error']=error; out['failed_at']=…; write_receipt(state_dir, out)` — it writes run-receipt.json. The amended goal now reads: 'a third run with the lock file held by a live PID exits 2 without processing, the run receipt (run-receipt.json) is byte-identical to before, and the refusal cause lands in a SEPARATE diagnostic file (last-lock-refusal.json) — fail-closed halts persist their cause without falsifying the success receipt.' `grep -c last-lock-refusal` over the plan returns 0: neither the ledger module, nor the orchestrator, nor g4-check.sh's check_5 (which asserts only third_run_lock_held_processed / stale_lock_reclaimed_and_ran / stale_then_next_acquire_wins) knows about it. As written the plan mutates the receipt on the lock-held path, so G4 item 5's 'receipt unchanged' assertion is unsatisfiable by construction. Note this also reverses part of round-1 G0A-4/G0B-6, which asked for the lock-held cause to be written to the receipt — the goal amendment supersedes that.
findings.fix: Split the lock-held path out of record_failure: write {error:'lock-held', refused_at, pid} to <state-dir>/last-lock-refusal.json and leave run-receipt.json untouched (client_state_gmail.py:319). Add the file to the State-dir layout line in the Interfaces block, assert byte-identity of run-receipt.json plus the presence of last-lock-refusal.json in g4-check.sh check_5, and add a negative fixture for it to g4-check.sh --selftest. Keep record_failure as-is for the gws/extraction/writer/budget/catch-all paths, which the goal still wants on the receipt.
